body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw full-donor \(\widehat\tau\). This equality is identified under event transport. Exact finite-sample conditional coverage and the asymptotic estimator and interval upper rates hold over every nonempty compatible \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), which requires \(B\ge D^2\) and imposes the two stated full-design centering restrictions. For each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), the four-channel risk and expected-length lower bounds match those upper rates, with constants allowed to depend on \(B-D^2\). For each fixed otherwise nonempty class with \(B=D^2\), only the treated, smoothing, and log-spacing lower channels are asserted; there is no universal donor converse. Historical response laws may be heterogeneous across units subject to boundedness and a common conditional mean; geometric beta mixing is imposed only on the design process. No sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering condition is imposed.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero. Only the stacked historical design process is geometrically beta mixing. This allows logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels. Unit response laws may be heterogeneous across and within cohorts, provided their historical conditional mean is the common \(m_s\); each unit's entire calendar response path is otherwise an unrestricted cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and standardized fourth-moment envelope \(B\); with \(D=Sd\), these conditions can define a nonempty class only when \(B\ge D^2\). Historical training coordinates are exact. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions for financial event-study estimators and explains that buy-and-hold comparisons require volatility matching.
The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.
The many-period--many-control result gives conditions for synthetic-control factor-loading recovery under imperfect pre-treatment fit.
The proximal synthetic-control theorems identify treatment effects by using excluded control outcomes as predetermined proxies.

body.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw local-polynomial estimator is exactly a cohort-weighted event coefficient. With \(D=Sd\), nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\). For every fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), matching bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\); for every fixed otherwise nonempty class with \(B=D^2\), exact coverage and the same four-term upper bounds remain valid, while the universal lower bound contains only treated, smoothing, and log-spacing channels. The feasible construction projects the full independent donor mean once, uses one normalized-shape local-polynomial fit per cohort, and combines bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding radii with exact Holder--Taylor and donor-modulus allowances. The proposed interval is conditionally honest in every finite sample throughout the compatible regime.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory mainly treats linear return contrasts; repeated-measurement regression fixes the query; generated-regressor theory typically moves training coordinates; and synthetic-control inference does not deliver a generated-event-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth under arbitrary relative growth.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture here observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, and generated-center uncertainty without a classical measurement-error inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact cohortwise weighted-panel coefficient representation, exact finite-sample conditional coverage over every compatible envelope, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers for each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\). For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), the estimator and interval upper bounds persist and the proved converse retains exactly the treated, smoothing, and log-spacing channels. A normalized Gram-shape selector under design-only geometric beta mixing, full-data bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding calibration, an exact Taylor allowance, full-sample covariance-standardized donor control, and channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish the result without donor splitting, sequential overlap, a dense-site condition, an upper local-mass condition, or identical unit response laws.

body.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching. Barber and Lyon (1997) and Mitchell and Stafford (2000) likewise motivate attention to dependence and compounding in long-horizon returns. Matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth; here that observation is motivation, not a theorem and not an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation, Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution, and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study local-polynomial regression evaluated at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer. Those experiments differ from the exact historical coordinates and single generated event query here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block-coupling template; here dependence is imposed only on the historical design. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for arbitrary relative growth, and Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies without deriving the generated-proxy minimax frontier. The present proof adds one full-donor center, heterogeneous bounded unit-response clusters with a common conditional mean, exact finite-sample conditional coverage, an explicit rare-block spacing witness, and the donor-envelope boundary qualification.
body.interpretation: For every integer \(T\ge3\), the replicated-smoothing term obeys \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), where \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\). Hence \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\). For each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), all three active components have matching lower witnesses: the oracle region has \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})\), the generated-proxy region reverses that relation, and the boundary equates the two. For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), the same upper phase map remains valid but a universal donor lower witness is not asserted, so only the treated and log-spacing active components are universally matched. The sole donor elbow in the upper rate and strict-slack frontier is \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball or anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The risk and honest-length results additionally use the two explicit full-design mean-stability and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence. Geometric beta mixing is required only for the historical design, and bounded unit response paths may otherwise be arbitrarily dependent over time and heterogeneous across units subject to their common conditional mean. Nonemptiness of the donor conditions requires \(B\ge D^2\). The universal donor converse uses fixed strict slack \(B-D^2>0\); at equality only the three non-donor lower channels are proved. The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass. The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp minimax constants.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification, the exact full-donor FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, a log-adjusted selector bound under design-only geometric beta mixing, a positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, compatible-envelope causal-panel lower embeddings, a conditional-risk frontier, and an exact finite-sample conditionally honest interval. For each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), four lower channels match the risk and expected-length upper rates, with constants allowed to depend on the fixed slack. For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), exact coverage and upper bounds remain, and the proved lower frontier contains treated, smoothing, and spacing channels but no universal donor converse; \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class. Historical and event unit response laws may be heterogeneous and each unit's calendar history is treated as one bounded cluster. No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, or temporal-outcome mixing condition is used. The mean-return dependence point retained in Related Work is motivation only, not an observational-equivalence theorem for the maintained full panel.
